bihar_raw_news.title: RJD announces candidates for six seats ahead of Bihar MLC polls
bihar_raw_news.content: Politics 11 Sep, 2026 RJD announces candidates for six seats ahead of Bihar MLC polls Business To Business, Patna, 11 September 2026: The Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) has intensified preparations for the upcoming elections to eight seats in the Bihar Legislative Council, announcing candidates for six constituencies while discussions over the remaining two are still underway. The elections will be held for four Teachers' Constituency and four Graduates' Constituency seats. The terms of the sitting MLCs are scheduled to expire on November 16, 2026, with the election process expected to be announced in September. Unlike Assembly elections, the Teachers' and Graduates' constituencies have a specialised electorate. While political parties are preparing their candidates, a number of Independent candidates are also expected to enter the contest. According to a list issued by the office of RJD state president Mangnilal Mandal, the party has named Dr Sanjiv Kumar Singh as its candidate for the Patna Teachers' Constituency and Dilip Kumar for the Patna Graduates' Constituency. The party has also fielded Nitesh Kumar from the Kosi Graduates' Constituency, Anil Kumar Jha from the Darbhanga Graduates' Constituency, Prof. Jayram Yadav from the Saran Teachers' Constituency and Dr Rashmi Vinayak Gautam from the Tirhut Graduates' Constituency. The RJD said discussions are continuing over the selection of candidates for the two remaining seats. Their names will be announced after the party finalises the candidates. With the tenure of the sitting MLCs approaching its end, political parties have stepped up preparations across the eight constituencies. The RJD has already outlined its strategy for several key seats, particularly in the Patna Teachers' and Graduates' constituencies. Among the four Teachers' Constituency seats, Prof. Naval Kishore Yadav of the BJP represents Patna, Dr Madan Mohan Jha of the Congress represents Darbhanga, Afaque Ahmad, an Independent, represents Saran, and Sanjay Kumar Singh of the CPI represents Tirhut. In the four Graduates' Constituencies, Neeraj Kumar of the JD(U) represents Patna, Sarvesh Kumar, an Independent, represents Darbhanga, NK Yadav of the BJP represents Kosi, and Banshidhar Brajvasi, an Independent, represents Tirhut, and their tenure will be completed in November this year. The specialised nature of the electorate is expected to make the contests different from conventional Assembly elections. Among the Teachers' Constituencies, Patna has the largest voter base with 16,689 registered voters, followed by Saran with 10,800, Tirhut with 9,204 and Darbhanga with 8,967 voters. The Graduates' Constituencies have substantially larger electorates. Tirhut has approximately 1.35 lakh voters, followed by Kosi with around 1.34 lakh, Darbhanga with nearly 1.27 lakh and Patna with about 88,000 voters. Alongside established political parties, Independent candidates are also preparing to campaign among teachers and graduates in their respective constituencies. bihar_raw_news.content: High-level review meeting regarding preparations for 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' concludes under chairmanship of Chief Secretary of Bihar ANI 11 Sep 2026, 22:29 GMT+10 Patna (Bihar) [India], September 11 (ANI): A high-level review meeting was held under the chairmanship of Bihar Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit to discuss the comprehensive preparations and successful implementation of the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan' (Service Pledge Campaign), scheduled to take place from September 17 to October 17. According to a press release, Principal Secretaries and Secretaries from various state departments attended the meeting in person, while District Magistrates from all districts joined via video conferencing. During the review, the Chief Secretary assessed the department-wise status of all 13 key components of the campaign and directed officials to complete preparations in a time-bound manner. The release noted that the campaign will commence on the evening of September 17 with the 'Aashirwad ka Diya' (Lamp of Blessing) program, involving the collective lighting of lamps in every household across the state and at a minimum of 10 prominent or symbolic public locations in each district. To facilitate this, lamps will be distributed to beneficiaries through Jeevika, urban local bodies, and the Public Distribution System. Additionally, between September 17 and October 7, painting and speech competitions based on the theme 'Viksit Bharat Sankalp' (Developed India Pledge) will be organised in all government and private schools under the 'Seva Chitra' initiative, alongside Parent-Teacher Meetings (PTMs). To raise public awareness, 18-20 theatre troupes will be formed under the 'Seva Smaran' (Service Remembrance) initiative; these troupes will perform street plays in schools, colleges, and panchayats, with special performances scheduled for October 2, the release said. Furthermore, a three-day event titled 'Aangan ka Milan' (Gathering in the Courtyard) will be held at all Anganwadi centres from September 25 to October 7. This event will feature the honouring of Anganwadi and ASHA workers, interactions with beneficiary mothers, and recreational activities for children, alongside the dissemination of information regarding nutrition and health schemes, the release added. To highlight the positive changes brought about in people's lives by government schemes, district and state-level digital data banks will be created by compiling authentic reels and short videos under the 'Kahani Badlav Ki' (Story of Change) component. Additionally, 'Seva Jyoti Yatra' will feature foot marches, as well as bicycle and motorcycle rallies across the state and districts; volunteers from 'Mera Yuva Bharat' will participate in these events, culminating in a collective pledge for 'Viksit Bharat 2047' (Developed India 2047). As the nationwide 'Vadnagar to Varanasi (Jal, Jan, aur Seva Sankalp Yatra)' passes through Bihar, arrangements will be made for grand receptions, security, accommodation, and interactions with local beneficiaries at designated stopover points, the release noted. To foster public participation, 25 activities, including the cleaning of ponds and Chhath ghats, tree plantation, and sanitation drives, will be conducted under the 'Seva Mera Yogdan' (Service: My Contribution) initiative, ensuring visible, on-ground transformation at a minimum of two locations in every assembly constituency. national_raw_news.content: The 18th BRICS Summit is set to begin at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today. The two-day grand event will bring together eleven major emerging and developing economies, including Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, India, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, and the UAE. During the high-level event, leaders of the BRICS member countries are expected to discuss key issues, including global governance, multilateralism, trade and investment, technology, food and energy security, healthcare, disaster resilience, and critical supply chains. The Summit is being held under India’s 2026 BRICS chairship, with the theme, “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.” Several key world leaders will participate in the high-profile Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be joined by Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali and Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan will also take part in the Summit. Brazil will be represented by Foreign Affairs Minister Mauro Vieira, while Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, will also attend. The Summit will begin with a closed session for BRICS member countries on “Inclusive Global Governance and Strengthening Multilateralism.” Leaders of the BRICS member countries will also visit the Bharat Innovates exhibition at Bharat Mandapam. This will be followed by a joint tree-planting ceremony and a gala dinner hosted by Prime Minister Modi. The Prime Minister is scheduled to hold a series of bilateral talks with BRICS leaders on the sidelines of the Summit today. These include meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping, Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed Ali, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung. New Delhi has taken centre stage for BRICS 2026, with world leaders converging at a time when there is global churn and instability. The Leaders meet at the backdrop of conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region, energy crisis, and climate change. BRICS has emerged as a key platform for coordinating economic policy among major emerging economies. It serves as the principal forum where these nations shape a common position on global governance. Through sustained dialogue, it has become a channel for advancing the interests of the Global South within multilateral institutions. Its agenda spans development, finance, technology, trade and people-to-people exchanges. The grouping reflects the growing economic weight and aspirations of emerging economies globally. India’s Chairship is guided by the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.” The theme places development, sustainability and innovation at the heart of the agenda. It also highlights the aspirations of the Global South.

national_raw_news.title: 45 mins ago | National 168 PM Modi calls for secure sea lanes and open supply routes to sustain global trade
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called for secure sea lanes, open supply routes and the safety of seafarers to sustain global trade. He also urged BRICS countries to work towards removing trade barriers and expanding opportunities for businesses. Mr Modi stated this while addressing Leaders’ Session of BRICS Business Forum at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi last evening. The Prime Minister said India was a strong advocate of freedom of navigation and the safety of seafarers, stressing that secure maritime routes were essential for the smooth movement of global trade. Amid rising trade barriers globally, Prime Minister Modi said India was seeking to build economic bridges. He said, India today offers a source of confidence for growth and stability. He called for Make in India, Innovate with India and Scale for the world. He said India has entered into Free Trade Agreements with nearly 40 countries since 2014, and stressed that its approach within BRICS was similarly focused on reducing barriers and expanding opportunities for businesses. The Prime Minister also highlighted initiatives such as the BRICS Incubator Network, BRICS MSME Portal and BRICS Startup Innovation Fund, aimed at connecting startups and small and medium enterprises with markets and finance. He called for greater exchanges of investment and talent among BRICS countries through these cooperation frameworks. Prime Minister Modi described BRICS countries as emerging centres of global innovation and solutions, with new possibilities taking shape from grassroots initiatives to frontier technologies. He said BRICS countries now represent 50 per cent of the world’s population, 40 per cent of global GDP and more than 25 per cent of global trade. He said that while global GDP has grown by around 2.5 times over the past two decades, the combined GDP of BRICS countries has increased by around 4.5 times, indicating that the bloc’s economic strength has grown at nearly twice the pace of the world economy. PM Modi noted that BRICS is celebrating 20 years this year. The grouping, which began with four countries in 2006, has expanded into a family of 21 BRICS and partner countries. Addressing the Forum, Russian President Vladimir Putin said that, over the last five years, more than 40 per cent of the world’s GDP has been produced by the BRICS countries. He said BRICS countries account for more than half of the world’s population, and that is why they have great, dynamic, vibrant domestic markets. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian suggested that one of the most important steps is to expand the use of national currencies in trade among the members. He said this step must be accompanied by the establishment of the necessary instruments for managing currency risks and reciprocal settlements. South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said the Global South must lead in manufacturing, Technology and value creation. He also raised concern over unilateral sanctions. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian suggested that one of the most important steps is to expand the use of national currencies in trade among the members. He said this step must be accompanied by the establishment of the necessary instruments for managing currency risks and reciprocal settlements. Brazilian Minister of Foreign Affairs Mauro Vieira said that, with its recent expansion, BRICS has consolidated itself as a platform connecting some of the world’s most dynamic and prosperous economies. He said that at a time when the global economy is facing threats from protectionism, economic coercion and unilateral sanctions, bringing productive sectors closer together is more relevant than ever. In his address, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said that, during India’s chairship, BRICS has been driven by a clear purpose – to achieve more balanced trade among member nations and explore the expansion of trade in services across the bloc. Mr Goyal said that, under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India remains committed to ensuring that this cooperation reaches those who form the backbone of BRICS economies. He said the cooperation must benefit farmers, empower women in business and beyond, and provide greater opportunities for wealth creation and prosperity to young entrepreneurs and micro, small and medium enterprises. national_raw_news.title: 46 mins ago | International 24 Saudi Arabia shuts major oil pipeline after drone attack
national_raw_news.content: Saudi Arabia said that it has shut down a major cross-country oil pipeline a day after it was attacked by drones. The statement by country’s Ministry of Energy said the East-West pipeline after it was attacked the day before. The statement called the shutdown a precautionary measure. The East-West pipeline has played a key role in Saudi Arabia’s ability to continue exporting oil following the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz during Iran’s war with the US and Israel. The Saudi Foreign Ministry blamed the attack on several drones that came from Iraq. The Iraqi government condemned the assault and ordered an investigation. The shutdown comes as Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen captured port of Mokha and a strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, at the southern entrance to the Red Sea, opening a new front in the ongoing West Asia conflict. The Bab el-Mandeb Strait is one of the world’s key shipping lanes. The advance could boost Iran’s strategy of driving up world oil and gas prices to pressure the United States. Two sources from the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised Yemeni government said its forces had pulled out of Perim and that the Houthis had also taken the ⁠mainland Red Sea coastal town of Dhubab, which faces the island. If the Houthis gain control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz, their backer Iran could gain a critical advantage in its war with the US, reducing supplies through a second major corridor and further raising oil prices. On the other hand, the 1,200-kilometer pipeline shut down by Saudi Arabia is the key alternative route for Kingdom’s oil to reach global markets, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. It has been shipping 4 million to 5 million barrels per day in recent months, amounting to 4 to 5 percent of global supply.

national_raw_news.title: 47 mins ago | National 181 PM Modi holds bilateral meetings with Russian President Putin, Iranian President, and UN chief Gu...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held bilateral meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and UN Secretary-General António Guterres in New Delhi yesterday ahead of the 18th BRICS Summit. During his meeting with President Vladimir Putin, the two leaders reviewed progress in India-Russia cooperation across a wide range of areas, including politics, trade and economy, defence, energy, space, skill mobility and people-to-people ties. Both sides also shared perspectives on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, including the conflicts in West Asia and the Black Sea region. Prime Minister Modi once again reiterated that dialogue and diplomacy was the way forward in resolving conflicts and India stood ready to assist in peace efforts. The two leaders agreed to remain engaged in an effort to strengthen further the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between the two countries. President Putin invited Prime Minister to visit Russia for the 24th India-Russia Annual Summit. The Prime Minister accepted the invitation. The dates of the Summit will be decided as per mutual convenience. Prime Minister Modi gifted Mr Putin a Russian translation of the Thirukkural, the ancient Tamil classic by poet-philosopher Thiruvalluvar, during their meeting. It has been published by the Central Institute of Classical Tamil. President Putin arrived in the national capital in the early hours yesterday to attend the BRICS Summit. In his meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Prime Minister Modi discussed bilateral relations and recent developments in West Asia. Mr Modi reiterated India’s consistent position that all issues must be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy. He stressed the need for continued efforts to ensure lasting peace and stability in the region, while also underlining the importance of safeguarding freedom of navigation and commerce and ensuring the safety and well-being of seafarers. The Prime Minister thanked Iran for its continued high-level participation in BRICS-related meetings and highlighted the grouping’s potential to promote resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability among countries of the Global South. Prime Minister Modi also met United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres. The two leaders discussed ongoing global conflicts, freedom of navigation, sustainable development, renewable energy, global food security and human-centric artificial intelligence. They also underlined the importance of strengthening multilateralism and reforming international institutions, including the United Nations Security Council, to reflect contemporary global realities. Mr Guterres congratulated Prime Minister Modi on India taking up the BRICS chairmanship for the fourth time.

national_raw_news.title: First-ever PIB press tour for Arunachal media concludes at Statue of Unity
national_raw_news.content: Echo Of Arunachal Newsflash State News First-ever PIB press tour for Arunachal media concludes at Statue of Unity EKTA NAGAR (GUJARAT), Sep 11: The first-ever Press Information Bureau (PIB) press tour for media representatives from Arunachal Pradesh concluded on Friday at Ekta Nagar, Gujarat, with a visit to the Statue of Unity and the Sardar Sarovar Dam. The nine-member media delegation visited the Statue of Unity, the world’s tallest statue, and the Sardar Sarovar Dam built across the Narmada River on the final day of the five-day exposure tour. The journalists paid floral tribute to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and undertook a guided tour of the Statue of Unity complex, including the viewing gallery and other facilities. They also interacted with Additional Collector Narayan Madhu, who briefed them on the development of Ekta Nagar and various initiatives undertaken in the region. The visit also featured an interaction with members of the Rathwa tribal community, providing an opportunity for cultural exchange between Arunachal Pradesh and Gujarat. The Arunachal journalists participated in traditional dances with members of the Rathwa community and exchanged greetings by presenting traditional scarves from Arunachal Pradesh. The five-day tour provided the delegation with exposure to Gujarat’s development initiatives across various sectors. The journalists visited the Dholera Greenfield Smart City, Sabarmati Multimodal Transport Hub, GIFT City and AMUL, gaining firsthand insights into developments in smart infrastructure, transportation, finance, technology and the dairy cooperative sector. The delegation also experienced Gujarat’s cultural heritage through participation in a traditional Garba performance. The tour provided the Arunachal media delegation with an opportunity to gain broader perspectives on India’s development journey while facilitating cultural interaction between the Northeast and western India. The exposure visit concluded with the delegation carrying back experiences and insights from Gujarat’s initiatives in infrastructure, technology, industry, cooperative development and cultural heritage.
